mandatoryComponents.description: These are the ONLY components that should be used. Do not create new ones.

ui.Button: Use for all clickable actions. Variants: default, destructive, outline, secondary, ghost, link
ui.Input: Use for all text inputs. Never create custom input components.
ui.Select: Use for all dropdown selections. Never create custom select components.
ui.Card: Use for all content containers. Variants: standard, elevated, nested
ui.Badge: Use for all status indicators. Never create custom status components.
ui.Table: Use for all tabular data. Never create custom table components.
ui.Dialog: Use for all modal interactions. Never create custom modal components.
ui.DropdownMenu: Use for all action menus. Never create custom menu components.
ui.Popover: Use for all floating content. Never create custom popover components.
ui.ScrollArea: Use for all scrollable content. Never create custom scroll components.
ui.Separator: Use for all visual divisions. Never create custom divider components.
ui.Skeleton: Use for all loading states. Never create custom loading components.
ui.Tooltip: Use for all hover information. Never create custom tooltip components.

icons.source: lucide-react ONLY. Never use other icon libraries.

prohibitedActions.noCustomComponents: Never create components that duplicate existing UI component functionality
prohibitedActions.noCustomHooks: Only create hooks for business logic, never for UI state that can be handled by existing patterns
prohibitedActions.noCustomStyles: Use only Tailwind classes defined in this schema. No custom CSS files.
prohibitedActions.noNewPatterns: Use only the patterns defined in this schema. Do not invent new layout patterns.
prohibitedActions.noLibraryMixing: Stick to the defined tech stack. Do not introduce new UI libraries.

beforeCreating: Check if existing component can be adapted with props
Check if existing pattern can be modified with different styling
Check if combination of existing components achieves the goal
Only create if absolutely no existing solution works

qualityAssurance.description: Mandatory quality checks before considering any implementation complete

typeScript: All props must have proper TypeScript interfaces
All data must be properly typed
Use proper generic types for reusable components
errorHandling: All async operations must have error handling
All data access must have null checks
All external API calls must have timeout handling
User-friendly error messages for all error states
performance: Use proper memoization for expensive calculations
Use server-side data fetching when possible
Optimize re-renders with proper dependency arrays

accessibility: All interactive elements must be keyboard accessible
All images must have alt text
All forms must have proper labels
Color cannot be the only way to convey information
responsiveness: Test on mobile, tablet, and desktop
Ensure touch targets are at least 44px
Text must be readable at all screen sizes
Tables must be horizontally scrollable on mobile
feedback: All actions must provide immediate feedback
Loading states for all async operations
Success/error messages for all form submissions

visual: Use only colors defined in the design system
Use only spacing values defined in the design system
Use only typography scales defined in the design system
Follow the exact component patterns defined
functional: All similar actions must behave the same way
All tables must have the same features
All forms must have the same validation patterns
All error states must look and behave the same

enforcementRules.description: These rules MUST be followed. No exceptions.
componentCreation: NEVER create a new component if an existing one can be adapted
NEVER create custom UI components that duplicate shadcn/ui functionality
NEVER create custom table components - use DataTable pattern only
NEVER create custom form components - use existing form patterns only
NEVER create custom modal components - use Dialog component only
styling: NEVER write custom CSS - use only Tailwind classes defined in this schema
NEVER use CSS modules or styled-components
NEVER create custom color values - use only design system colors
patterns: NEVER deviate from the mandatoryStructure for tables
NEVER create custom layout patterns - use only defined layouts
NEVER create custom loading states - use Skeleton or Loader2 only
NEVER create custom error states - use defined error patterns only

colorTheme: Use bg-[#F2F3F4] as the primary background for cards and main content areas
Apply bg-[#F8F9FA] for nested content or secondary panels within cards
Use bg-[#FAFBFC] for dialog bodies and highlighted sections
Implement elevated surfaces (bg-white/90) for modals and floating elements
Combine backgrounds with appropriate borders (border-slate-200/60) for definition
Use color variants (blue, green, amber, red) sparingly for status indicators and important metrics
Always provide dark mode equivalents for all background colors
Maintain consistent opacity levels (50-90%) for visual hierarchy
dialogDesign: Always include a clear title and description
Provide a way to close the dialog (X button or Cancel)
Use consistent button ordering (Cancel on left, primary action on right)
For large dialogs, use a fixed header and footer with scrollable content
For complex forms, consider a multi-step approach
Always show loading states during async operations
Use elevated backgrounds (bg-white/90) for dialog headers and footers
Apply subtle backgrounds (bg-[#FAFBFC]) for dialog bodies
formDesign: Provide helper text for complex fields
Use appropriate input types (date pickers, selects, etc.)
Consider using grid layouts for dense forms
tableDesign: ARCHITECTURE: Use server-side data fetching with URL state management for scalability
LAYOUT: Always wrap tables in rounded-md border containers for visual definition
STYLING: Use bg-muted/50 for table headers to distinguish from data rows
INTERACTION: Apply hover:bg-muted/30 to data rows for interactive feedback
SEARCH: Include comprehensive text search in toolbar with proper debouncing
FILTERING: Implement faceted filters for categorical data with multi-select capability
ACTIONS: Use consistent row actions with dropdown menus containing categorized actions
PAGINATION: Implement pagination for datasets with >50 items with page size options
SORTING: Allow column sorting where appropriate with clear visual indicators (arrows)
LOADING: Use skeleton loaders or loading states during data fetching
EMPTY STATES: Provide helpful empty states with icons and clear action buttons
ERROR HANDLING: Include error states with retry mechanisms and clear error messages
SPACING: Use consistent cell padding (p-4) for readability and visual balance
RESPONSIVE: Implement mobile-first design - hide less important columns on mobile
ANALYTICS: Add dashboard cards above tables when showing key metrics (4-column grid)
COMPLEX FILTERING: Use sidebar layouts for advanced filtering requirements
PAGE STRUCTURE: Maintain consistent spacing between page header, dashboard, and table (gap-6)
STATE MANAGEMENT: Synchronize all table state (filters, sorting, pagination) with URL parameters
ACCESSIBILITY: Ensure full keyboard navigation and screen reader support
PERFORMANCE: Use proper memoization and avoid loading all data client-side
COLUMN TYPES: Implement standardized column patterns (selection, identifier, status, date, actions)
STATUS BADGES: Use color-coded badges with consistent color mapping across the application
ACTION MENUS: Structure action menus with logical grouping and separators
CONDITIONAL ACTIONS: Show actions only when relevant (e.g., View Signature if signature exists)
DESTRUCTIVE ACTIONS: Always separate destructive actions and use appropriate styling
NULL SAFETY: Implement proper null checks and fallback values for all data fields
TYPE SAFETY: Use TypeScript throughout for better developer experience and fewer runtime errors
iconUsage: Use icons consistently across similar components
Pair icons with text for better clarity
Keep icon sizes consistent within contexts
Use color to enhance meaning, not as the sole indicator

postImplementation: ✓ All table states work correctly (loading, empty, error)
✓ All filters and search functionality work
✓ All actions in dropdown menus work
✓ Page is responsive on mobile, tablet, and desktop
✓ Visual consistency with other pages confirmed

migrationGuide.description: How to migrate existing tables to the new pattern
steps: 1. Create [Entity]Client wrapper component using the template
2. Update DataTable component to accept onFiltersChange and onPageChange props
3. Update DataTableToolbar to accept and use onFiltersChange prop
4. Update DataTableFacetedFilter to accept and use onValueChange prop
5. Update DataTablePagination to accept and use onPageChange prop
6. Update page.tsx to use the new client wrapper
7. Test URL state persistence and filter functionality
migrationGuide.compatibility: This pattern is backward compatible - existing tables will continue to work without the new props
